_om: Veckans publiceringar (Admin → Artiklar → Veckans publiceringar; api/routers/blog_week.py). En rad per planerad publicering ur PUBLICERINGSPLAN.md avsnitt 2 (spår P tisdag och fredag kl. 07.00) och avsnitt 1 (spår F). Fält: datum (ÅÅÅÅ-MM-DD) och tid (TT:MM) i svensk tid, Europe/Stockholm, sommar- och vintertid sköts av sig själv; id = artikelns Firestore-id (samlingen posts, syns i Admin); titel = arbetsrubrik för listan (artikelns egen rubrik gäller); spar = "P" (populärspåret) eller "F" (forskningsspåret); bluesky = {"text": engelsk text, "tags": [utan #]} eller null för inget inlägg – texten med taggarna högst 300 tecken (scripts/bluesky_post.compose), länken går till den engelska utgåvan; taggmönster: ämnestagg + #MedievalSky/#Skystorians varannan gång + fler forskartaggar + #VikingAge + #Vikings; godkand = null tills Viktor godkänner, sedan tiden (ISO) då veckan godkändes. Vid godkännandet schemaläggs artikeln (samma väg som Schemalägg i Admin, med säkerhetskopia), Bluesky-inlägget läggs i data/bluesky/ko.json med publiceringsdagen som datum (före andra inlägg samma dag, så att det går ut kl. 18 samma dag; resten av kön skjuts en dag) och godkand fylls i. En artikel som redan är publicerad eller schemalagd, eller vars tid har passerat, rörs inte. Lägg till nya veckor här, i datumordning.

poster.titel: Ingen på runstenarna hette Freja – i dag heter 7 000 svenskar det

bluesky.text: No one on Sweden's runestones was called Freja. Today 7,000 Swedes are. We counted every Old Norse first name in use now: the stones' names are ageing with their bearers, while the gods' names (Freja, Idun, Embla, Loke) grow.

poster.titel: De gamla landen: Skåne – slätten där kungen byggde nytt

bluesky.text: New in the series The old lands: Skåne around AD 1000, a Danish land in change. Uppåkra fades, the king builds ring forts and a church in Lund. From the shore at Trelleborg to the land assembly east of Lund.

poster.titel: Runstenarna stod vid lerans kant – men halva gåtan är olöst

bluesky.text: We laid the soil map over every runestone still in place. The stones stand not on the clay but at its edge, on dry ground near the grave fields. And half of the Mälaren valley's lead is explained by neither soil, settlement nor water.

poster.titel: Fyra stenar för två barn – släkterna som går att följa över runstenarna

bluesky.text: Four stones for two children. Testing names against chance, we linked 42 families across 95 runestones. Nine in ten links are already in the runologists' list. Of three new ones, one is probably wrong.

poster.titel: De gamla landen: Attundaland – där man gjorde sina tingsplatser

bluesky.text: Gerlög outlived her daughter Inga and inherited from her – cut into the rock at Hillersjö. The old lands: Attundaland around AD 1000, where great men wrote in stone that they had made the assembly place.

poster.titel: Den goda döden – vad runstenarna säger om hur de dog

bluesky.text: Only one Swedish runestone in sixteen says how the dead died: battle, betrayal, a sinking ship, a mother of small children, men in white christening robes. After 1050 the stones tell of death half as often.

poster.titel: De gamla landen: Fjädrundaland – folklandet längst in i havsviken

bluesky.text: In Fjädrundaland, western Uppland, one runestone in three bears a cross, against six in ten in the rest of Uppland. Balle's stone for Brune, who "died in christening robes", has none either.

poster.titel: Döda i vita kläder – sju runstenar över dem som dog nydöpta

bluesky.text: Seven runestones, all in Uppland, say the dead man died 'in white clothes' – in his baptismal robes, newly baptised. On four of the five where the raisers can be read, a woman is among them: his mother or his wife.

poster.titel: Vikingarnas österled – eller bara Ingvars?

bluesky.text: 25 Swedish runestones remember one journey: Ingvarr's expedition to Serkland. We took them out, under a plan locked in advance. About half of the stones' eastward lead vanished – yet they still look east more than the Icelanders' sagas.

poster.titel: Asatron i landskapet – gudarnas socknar var gravarnas socknar

bluesky.text: Odensvi, Torsåker, Ullvi: the old gods live on in Swedish place names. Cult-place names are thickest around Lake Mälaren, and hardly any parish with one lacks an Iron Age grave field.

poster.titel: Fyra runstensfynd prövade mot hundra års invändningar – två står, ett försvagas, ett väntar på kartorna

bluesky.text: Research report: we tested four of our own runestone findings against a century of objections, under plans locked in advance. Two stand, one weakens (the east share without Ingvarr's 25 stones), one awaits the old maps.

poster.titel: De gamla landen: Gotland – ett eget land mitt i havet

bluesky.text: New in the series The old lands: Gotland around AD 1000. A land of its own in the sea: farms that moved about their land, harbours along the whole coast, more silver in the ground than anywhere else, one assembly for the island.

poster.titel: Läs om du kan – kunde vikingatidens folk läsa runstenarna?

bluesky.text: Could Viking-age people read the runestones? One in three Swedish runestones points at itself – 'this stone' – and one in nine names its carver. But only ten of 2,321 ask outright for a reader: interpret, he who can.

poster.titel: Vikingarnas jul fanns i sagorna – men inte på en enda runsten

bluesky.text: Merry Christmas from Vitki! The word jól occurs 81 times in Heimskringla: feasts, gifts, killings and a king who moved Yule to the Christian date. On the runestones: not once. And Júli on Sö 362? Named after a hedgehog.

poster.titel: De gamla landen: Värend – sjöbygden mitt i skogen

bluesky.text: New in the series The old lands: Värend, the largest of Småland's small lands. A lake country ringed by forest around AD 1000: large villages, a great mound at Ingelstad and perhaps an assembly by Helgasjön.

poster.titel: Mö, dotter eller flicka? Ordet som kunde betyda ogift

bluesky.text: On a grave slab in Skänninge, Åsa is called both daughter and maiden. The rare runic word for maiden appears on just 4 of 2,320 Swedish runestones – and it seems to have meant an unmarried woman, not a young girl.

poster.titel: Borgarna vid vattnet – vad var fornborgarna?

bluesky.text: Sweden has 1,304 Iron Age hillforts; only 73 are listed as excavated. 64% lie within 500 m of the water, against 48% of the hills around them. In the legends they became homes of giants.

poster.titel: De gamla landen: Möre – kusten vid sundet

bluesky.text: New in the series The old lands: Möre, the coast by the Kalmar Sound around AD 1000. Fertile clay between forest and sea, villages by the rivers, ships offshore – a land judged by Östergötland's law, not by that of Småland's Tiohärad.

poster.titel: Hundra år av runfrågor I: Grundläggarna som ställde frågorna vi fortfarande ställer

bluesky.text: We read Fornvännen from its first volume in 1906. Part I: the founders – von Friesen, Brate, Lindqvist, Wessén, Jansson – who mended stones, hunted lost ones in church walls and asked our questions.

poster.titel: Bakhäll, bro och kvarnsten – runstenarnas andra liv

bluesky.text: A runestone became a baking slab for soldiers and cracked in the rain. Another lay as a bridge for 200 years, a third was cut into a millstone. The stones' second lives, from the old editions.

poster.titel: De gamla landen: Finnveden – landet längs Lagan

bluesky.text: Along the river Lagan in Finnveden almost every grave was a mound. At Fallnaveka two people were buried with two horses, two dogs, two pigs, sheep and goat. The old lands: western Småland around AD 1000.

poster.titel: Hundra år av runfrågor II: När forskarna började räkna

bluesky.text: From 1970 runologists began to count – and to argue about how. Part II: a Varangian's name in Hagia Sophia, a generous quarrel over statistics, Futhark as a journal, and the Rök stone read anew.

poster.titel: Vendeltid, vikingatid, medeltid – fanns gränserna?

bluesky.text: Did the Viking Age end in 1066? In Sweden runestones went on for decades: nearly a third of those with a firm style group are later. Around 1100 the runes moved into the churches and onto grave slabs.

poster.titel: Prickarna, åsrunan och tiden

bluesky.text: Viking-age carvers had 16 runes for some 30 sounds, so some added a dot: i became e. In Götaland dotted runes go with crosses. In Uppland dots stayed rare, while the ós-rune spread on the late stones.

poster.titel: Kan man räkna sig fram till vikingarna?

bluesky.text: Can you count your way to the Vikings? One runestone cannot tell you whether it is unusual; all 2,321 together can. How Vitki locks its questions before counting, and says where the numbers fall short.

poster.titel: Vem höll i mejseln? Vad Vitki ser av ristarnas handlag – och vad den inte ser

bluesky.text: Who held the chisel? 3 in 4 Swedish runestones have no known carver. Vitki learns carvers' traits from signed stones only, right first on 71 % of them – but a hand with no name still lands in a known workshop.

poster.titel: Så gör du: mät runorna, inte ormen

bluesky.text: How do you measure how a runestone's runes were cut, and not the serpent around them? A step-by-step guide to Vitki's groove analysis on M 15 at Skön, Medelpad: face the carved side, check the bands, count with the rune as the unit.

poster.titel: Hundra år av runfrågor III: Stenarna som ingen skrev om

bluesky.text: Which runestones have scholars written about? Part III: just over half of Sweden's runestones are never mentioned by number in the journals. Not province or period decides, but how long the text is and whether the stone survives.

poster.titel: Fornnordiska väsen – Var tog alverna vägen?

bluesky.text: Where did the elves go? We read all 64 elves in Old Norse literature. In the Edda they stand beside the gods, in the sagas never – and in Sweden they are all but absent from place names and runestones. Old Norse beings, part 2.

poster.titel: Ristarna utan namn

bluesky.text: Many runestones were carved by the same unknown hand. A model now points out such groups – and in a locked test it put the runologists' own same-hand pairs together six times as often as neighbouring stones.

poster.titel: Fornnordiska väsen – Jättekvinnans ugn

bluesky.text: The giants of Old Norse literature: named jötnar in the Edda, trolls in the sagas – and in Swedish place names they cling to the oldest graves. Old Norse beings, part 3.

poster.titel: Fornnordiska väsen – Var sjätte runsten bär en björn

bluesky.text: 375 of 2,321 Swedish runestones carry a bear name – Bjôrn, Þorbjôrn, Ásbjôrn – twice as many as the wolf names. In the sagas the bear is a rare word. Old Norse beings, part 4.

poster.titel: Fornnordiska väsen – Draken var ett skepp

bluesky.text: In saga prose the word dreki means a ship in 78 per cent of cases. In the Eddic poems the dragon is ormr. On the runestones the serpent winds round the text on three stones in four – but is never named. Old Norse beings, part 5.

poster.titel: Så läser vi rundjuren

bluesky.text: How do you count a rune animal? Two independent readers, a fixed codebook – and every kind of picture tested against another. The 17th- and 18th-century drawings held for the animal's main features; the depth images from 3D scans did not.

poster.titel: Fornnordiska väsen – Valkyriorna göts i Birka

bluesky.text: Some thirty clay moulds for small silver women lie in Birka's black earth – the 'valkyries'. We followed norns, dísir, valkyries and fylgjur through the Edda and the sagas. Old Norse beings, part 6.

poster.titel: Fornnordiska väsen – Vargarna i Gunnars dröm

bluesky.text: In the sagas the wolf is hardly ever an animal. Half of the time it is a human being – usually an enemy seen in a dream. Old Norse beings, part 7.

poster.titel: Fornnordiska väsen – De döda som kom hem

bluesky.text: At Fróðá in Iceland the dead sat by the fire every evening, until the living took them to court. In Old Norse literature the dead come home almost only in the sagas of Icelanders. Old Norse beings, part 8.

poster.titel: Runstenar med samma hand

bluesky.text: New research report: a model groups runestones that may share a carver – also where no named carver fits. In a locked final test, 42 % of the runologists' own same-hand pairs landed in the same group, against 7 % for neighbouring stones.

poster.titel: En upptäcktsmotor för runstenarna

bluesky.text: New research report: a discovery engine that searches one half of the runestones for unexpected associations, freezes the list and tests it on the other half. Of 28 associations found in the first half, 14 held in the second.

poster.titel: Skrivmiljöer utan namn

bluesky.text: New research report: runestones without a carver grouped by how they are written. Tested on known carvers, a group is on average 86 % the same carver, against 71 % for nearby stones – but that the unsigned groups are one hand is not shown.
